name: Raspberry Pi Pico
description: RP2040 board (dual Cortex-M0+ at 125 MHz, 264 KB RAM, 2 MB flash) at 3.3 V logic, 51 × 21 mm. Runs real arduino-pico firmware on rp2040js: GPIO, PWM, ADC, UART, I2C, SPI, PIO and USB serial. GPIO ids are GP0 to GP28 (the number you use in pinMode); GP25 drives the on-board LED. 3.3 V only: 5 V on a GPIO damages it.

pins.label: GP0
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO0; McuBackend pin "GP0" (pinMode(0, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM0A, SPI0 RX (MISO), UART0 TX, I2C0 SDA, PIO. Serial1 TX by default.

pins.label: VBUS
pins.description: USB 5 V (VBUS), straight from the USB connector. Stamped as a 5 V source (USB power assumed). Use it for 5 V parts, never on a GPIO.

pins.label: VSYS
pins.description: Main system input (1.8 to 5.5 V) that feeds the 3.3 V buck-boost regulator; from VBUS through a Schottky diode, about 4.7 V on USB. Stamped as 4.7 V. A battery goes here (through a diode if USB is also connected).

pins.label: GND
pins.description: Ground (all GND pins are one node).

pins.label: 3V3_EN
pins.description: Enable of the 3.3 V regulator, pulled up on the board; tie to GND to switch 3.3 V off. Not simulated (the 3V3 rail is always on).

pins.label: 3V3
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board RT6150 buck-boost regulator. Keep the load under 300 mA. Stamped as a 3.3 V source.

pins.label: ADC_VREF
pins.description: ADC reference, 3.3 V through a 200 Ω filter resistor. Usable as a quiet reference for potentiometers. The simulated ADC always uses 3.3 V as its reference.
